messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient, a 46-year-old male, was admitted in 2006 with a 3.7 mm skin cancer on his left forearm. He had multiple recurrences which were treated with surgical resections, topical imiquimod, and intra-tumour IL-2 as per protocol. The patient was enrolled in IMM-101-001 study which resulted in a decreased rate of new disease however his condition worsened with lung metastases developed. Subsequently, he received ipilimumab on a clinical trial which showed a remarkable response, with most of the lesions resolving and a couple of visceral lesions remaining stable over 5 years.  
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
CONDITION AT DISCHARGE:
Stable with no acute problems.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
The patient is advised to follow up for further evaluation to monitor his health status. 

FOLLOW-UP RECOMMENDATIONS:
A follow-up with a specialist is recommended for ongoing care. 

MEDICATIONS:
None.

FUTURE TREATMENT PLAN:
To be decided upon specialist consultation. 

SUMMARY:
The patient, a 46-year-old male, was admitted with a 3.7 mm skin cancer on his left forearm that had recurred several times. He was treated with surgical resections, topical imiquimod and intra-tumour IL-2, however, his condition worsened and he was enrolled in a clinical trial. The patient received ipilimumab and had a remarkable response, with most of the lesions resolving and a couple of visceral lesions stable over 5 years. The patient will follow up with a specialist for ongoing care and treatment planning.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
This is most consistent with melanoma: a skin cancer on the forearm treated with imiquimod and intra-tumour IL-2, then ipilimumab, which is a melanoma therapy. The 3.7 mm size reads as a Breslow thickness. The diagnosis section is withheld, so this is an inference from the treatment history.

The principal diagnosis could be the primary melanoma of the skin (C43) or the secondary lung and visceral metastases (C78 or C79). The admission was for the skin cancer, and the metastases are described as a later development. I chose C43 on that basis.

C43
